earlier_scan.note: Only Glottolog resource is Keraf 1978 comparative wordlist (Daftar Kata Dasar); no description of Lamatuka phonology/stress located.

sources.citation: Grimes, Charles E. & Owen Edwards. 2026 [2025]. The Austronesian languages of eastern Indonesia and Timor-Leste: Unravelling their prehistory and classification. Berlin: Language Science Press.
sources.note: Only an areal remark, sec. 3.2 p. 115: 'While penultimate stress is the normal rule for Wallacean languages, words with penultimate schwa can have stress on other syllables' (about Flores languages generally). Lamatuka [lmq] appears only in the Lamaholot classification tree (p. 166, East Lamaholot with Lewo Eleng [lwe]), in comparative lexical tables, and in fn. 22 p. 137 (lexicostatistics from Keraf 1978:448). No Lamatuka-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page lama1279 (refs Fricke 2019 pp. 171-228; Grimes & Edwards 2025 pp. 116-122; Ethnologue) and Glottolog reference record 127725 (Keraf 1978 Daftar Kata Dasar, 31 lects incl. Lamatuka, type overview/wordlist).
sources.note: Bibliographic only: no grammar, sketch or phonology listed for Lamatuka (Glottolog lists no grammar, sketch or phonology); alt name Lamatoka; status threatened.

sources.citation: Krausse, Daniel. 2016. A brief grammar sketch of Eastern Atadei (Atadei Painara), Lembata (MA-level sketch), as held in catalog src for sout2896.
sources.note: Lists Lamatuka among SIL's eight Lembata languages (from Grimes 1978) and notes Keraf 1978 covered it; its own stress remarks concern Eastern Atadei (a Central Lamaholot variety), not Lamatuka.

sources.citation: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Daftar Kata Dasar. In Morfologi Dialek Lamalera, 406-447. Jakarta: Universitas Indonesia (also Ende: Arnoldus). Lamatuka 200-item wordlist as digitized in LexiRumah 3, lect lama1277-lamat.
sources.note: 202 wordlist forms, all source keraf1978; IPA-ish transcription with nasal vowels and schwa, zero stress marks. The original print monograph was not accessible (UI library search rejected; not on archive.org/HathiTrust/Google Books preview).

sources.citation: Kotan, Rosa Delima Rosari Buti, Fransiskus Bustan & Zantty O. Padahana. 2025. Textual and Contextual Meanings of Peni and Nogo Folklore in Lembata Language. SPARKLE Journal of Language, Education and Culture 7(1): 54-62. Kupang: Universitas Nusa Cendana.
sources.note: No phonology content: ethnolinguistic (textual/contextual meaning) analysis of a folklore book; no transcription of Lamatuka speech, no remarks on sounds, stress or tone.

sources.citation: Nugroho, Zefanya Christiady & Heppy Christinawati Silaen. 2024. Dinamika ketahanan bahasa-bahasa rumpun Lamaholot di Lembata. Linguistik Indonesia 42(1): 221-245. doi:10.26499/li.v42i1.578
sources.note: Participatory language-vitality survey of seven Lembata Lamaholot languages including Lamatuka (desa Lamatuka, EGIDS 6a -> 6b). Sociolinguistic only; nothing on phonology or stress. Its reference list names no phonological description of Lamatuka (only Keraf 1978, Fricke 2017/2019).

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna. 2023. The mixed lexicon of Lamaholot (Austronesian): A language with a large lexical component of unknown origin. Chapter 5 in Marian Klamer & Francesca R. Moro (eds.), Traces of Contact in the Lexicon: Austronesian and Papuan Studies. Leiden: Brill. doi:10.1163/9789004529458 (open access; archive.org item oapen-20.500.12657-87067).
sources.note: No phonology of Lamatuka: the chapter is about lexical strata (AN vs non-AN lexemes); Lamatuka appears in Table 5.8 (69 AN / 59 non-AN of 128 lexemes) and in lexeme sets. A full-text search of the whole volume for stress/accent finds hits only in chapters on Javanese, Rote-Meto, Nimboran, Tagalog and Ilokano. The companion chapter by Moro, Sulistyono & Kaiping cites Lamatuka prita 'dirty' (fn. 6) -- lexical only.

sources.citation: Klamer, Marian & Francesca R. Moro (eds.). 2023. Traces of Contact in the Lexicon: Austronesian and Papuan Studies. Leiden/Boston: Brill. DOI 10.1163/9789004529458. (incl. ch. 6: Schapper, Antoinette & Juliette Huber, 'Entwined Histories: The Lexicons of Kawaimina and Maka Languages', 180-209; ch. 8: Gerstner-Link, Claudia, 'Multilateral Lexical Transfer among Four Papuan Language Families: Border, Nimboran, Sentani, and Sko', 263-306; ch. 3 Klamer on Timor-Alor-Pantar/Austronesian contact, 57-100; ch. 5 Fricke on Lamaholot, 140-179; ch. 7 Moro, Sulistyono & Kaiping on Alorese, 213-262.)
sources.note: Lexical-stratum percentages (ch. 5) and word forms ('it is Lamaholot Lamatuka which has prita for "dirty"', p252-3); no prosodic statement anywhere in chs. 5 or 7.

sources.citation: Fricke, Hanna L.A. 2019. Traces of language contact: The Flores-Lembata languages in eastern Indonesia. LOT Dissertation Series 544. Utrecht: LOT (Leiden PhD).
sources.note: Sec. 3.2.5 (pp. 49-50) gives a stress rule (penultimate unless the penult has schwa, then ultimate) for Central Lembata, a Central Lamaholot variety coded ISO lvu (Kalikasa, Atadei district) -- not Lamatuka. Sec. 4.1.5 (p. 160): Eastern Lamaholot (varieties Lewoeleng and Lamatuka) 'remains largely undescribed'; the only materials are Keraf's (1978) two 200-item wordlists. Table 4.2 (p. 162) lists 'lmt lmq Lamatuka Keraf 1978b' under Eastern Lamaholot. No statement on Lamatuka stress anywhere in the text (a full-text search for stress/accent hits only CL).

sources.citation: Keraf, Gregorius. 1978. Morfologi Dialek Lamalera. Doctoral dissertation, Universitas Indonesia, Jakarta; also published Ende, Flores: Arnoldus. (Full monograph incl. the Lamaholot dialect-survey chapter and the 'Daftar Kata Dasar' pp. 406-447 with the Lamatuka list; lexicostatistic table p. 448.)

sources.note: The only primary source containing Lamatuka data; the full monograph (not just the wordlist) may carry orthographic/phonological remarks on the surveyed Lembata dialects, though its grammatical description is of Lamalera, not Lamatuka. Print only; the LexiRumah digitization of the Lamatuka list carries no stress marks.
